sentinels.derived: computed from other quantities in this project
sentinels.measured_here: measured by this project from deposited coordinates
sentinels.method_choice: an algorithmic choice, not a measured quantity
sentinels.convention: a community convention rather than a measurement
sentinels.unverified: value in use but its source could not be confirmed

parameters.name: Bending modulus
parameters.source_note: 20-25 k_BT for a typical bilayer; 20 used for PIEZO1
parameters.description: Helfrich bending rigidity of the bilayer.

parameters.name: Resting membrane tension
parameters.source_note: 0.1 k_BT/nm^2 = 0.42 mN/m, a mildly tensioned membrane
parameters.description: Lateral tension entering the Helfrich functional.

parameters.name: Small-slope validity limit
parameters.source_note: the Monge expansion drops terms of order |grad h|^2, so at slope 0.5 the neglected terms are already ~25%
parameters.description: Slope above which the linearised solver is flagged.

parameters.name: PIEZO1 dome contact slope
parameters.source_note: a/sqrt(R^2-a^2) from the fitted 7WLT cap; 63 degrees
parameters.description: Slope where the dome meets the flat bilayer.

parameters.name: Intrinsic gating free energy
parameters.source_note: fitted with dA = 8 nm^2 to give T50 = 5.1 mN/m
parameters.description: Closed-to-open free energy at zero tension.

parameters.name: Gating area change
parameters.source_note: 8 +- 1 nm^2 from Boltzmann fits to tension-response
parameters.description: In-plane area change on opening.

parameters.name: Published closed dome radius
parameters.source_note: the regression target for our geometry pipeline
parameters.description: Radius of curvature of the closed-state dome.

parameters.name: Tension midpoint
parameters.source_note: four-state TENSION model
parameters.description: Rate midpoint.

parameters.name: Tension sensitivity
parameters.source_note: exponential tension scale
parameters.description: e-fold tension for the rate constants.

parameters.name: C->O rate prefactor
parameters.source_note: k1 = 5.1 exp(sigma/b)
parameters.description: Opening rate at zero tension.

parameters.name: O->C rate prefactor
parameters.description: Closing rate.

parameters.name: O->I1 rate
parameters.description: Inactivation entry.

parameters.name: I1->O rate
parameters.description: Inactivation exit.

parameters.name: I1->I2 rate prefactor
parameters.source_note: k3 = 34.6 exp(-sigma/b)
parameters.description: Deep-inactivation entry.

parameters.name: I2->C rate
parameters.description: Recovery.

parameters.name: C->I2 rate
parameters.source_note: k-3 follows by microscopic reversibility rather than being fitted
parameters.description: Reverse recovery.

parameters.name: Unitary conductance
parameters.source_note: 25-30 pS; also Vaisey & MacKinnon 2026
parameters.description: Single-channel conductance.

parameters.name: Wild-type inactivation tau
parameters.source_note: whole-cell; mutants are calibrated by FOLD CHANGE against this, never by absolute tau across preparations
parameters.description: Reference inactivation time constant.

parameters.name: Measured half-activation tension
parameters.source_note: 2.7 +- 0.1 mN/m cell-attached
parameters.description: Validation target for the emergent T50.

parameters.name: Spring cutoff
parameters.source_note: the usual choice for large membrane proteins
parameters.description: C-alpha pairs closer than this are connected.

parameters.name: Inverse-power spring scale
parameters.source_note: distance scale in gamma ~ (d0/d)^2; reproduces measured fluctuations better than a uniform cutoff
parameters.description: Reference distance for distance-weighted springs.

parameters.name: Spring constant
parameters.source_note: sets the energy scale only; overlaps and mode shapes are invariant to it
parameters.description: Uniform spring stiffness.

parameters.name: Modes to solve
parameters.source_note: the first 6 per connected component are rigid-body and are discarded
parameters.description: Number of low modes.

parameters.name: C3 character tolerance
parameters.source_note: how close a rotation character must sit to +1 to call a mode A-symmetric
parameters.description: Symmetry labelling tolerance.

parameters.name: Protomers
parameters.source_note: PIEZO1 is a C3 homotrimer
parameters.description: Subunits in the assembly.

parameters.name: Slice spacing
parameters.source_note: sampling at 1 A resolves the CTD constrictions, which are ~1 A wide
parameters.description: Spacing of slices along the conduction axis.

parameters.name: Probe leash
parameters.source_note: MANDATORY: without it the clearance function has no interior maximum and the answer escapes to ~6000 A
parameters.description: Maximum probe offset from the axis.

parameters.name: Search radius
parameters.source_note: wide enough to include every atom that could bound the probe at the leash limit
parameters.description: Neighbour radius when maximising clearance.

parameters.name: Constriction threshold
parameters.source_note: a local minimum narrower than this is a candidate gate
parameters.description: Radius below which a minimum is reported.

parameters.name: Conducting ion radius
parameters.source_note: HOLE's convention for a permeant cation
parameters.description: Radius a pore must exceed to pass an ion sterically.

parameters.name: Dewetting energy threshold
parameters.source_note: 1 RT; the contour CHAP draws
parameters.description: Water free energy above which a residue is flagged.

parameters.name: Closed-gate score cutoff
parameters.source_note: optimal cutoff from their ROC analysis, AUROC 0.91
parameters.description: Sum-of-distances above which a channel is called closed.

parameters.name: Hydrophobicity bandwidth
parameters.source_note: CHAP's default; the landscape was built with it, so changing it indexes the grid with a different coordinate
parameters.description: Gaussian kernel width along the pore axis.

parameters.name: Water molecule radius
parameters.source_note: below this a pore is shut sterically and the wetting question does not arise
parameters.description: Water radius.

parameters.name: Scored pore radius limit
parameters.source_note: CHAP restricts the score to residues lining the narrow part (0.7 nm)
parameters.description: Widest slice that is scored.

parameters.name: AlphaFold confidence threshold
parameters.source_note: AlphaFold's own banding calls 70-90 confident and below 70 low; the project adopts that boundary rather than choosing its own, so the reported confident fraction means what a reader of AlphaFold DB expects
parameters.description: pLDDT at or above which a predicted residue is treated as placed.

parameters.name: Hybrid graft anchor window
parameters.source_note: the graft is anchored on residues NEAR the seam, not on the whole overlap: fitting all 1279 shared residues gives 19.0 A RMSD because the AlphaFold and cryo-EM blades are different conformations, and spreading that error into the join misplaces the graft. A 200-residue window uses 110 residues and fits to 2.4 A
parameters.description: Residues either side of the seam used to place the predicted distal blade.

parameters.name: Sphere-fit trim fraction
parameters.source_note: worst-fitting points ignored, so a few outlying helices do not drag the fitted curvature
parameters.description: Fraction of points trimmed when fitting the sphere.

parameters.name: Radial profile bins
parameters.source_note: 40 bins over a ~10 nm dome gives ~2.5 A resolution, finer than the C-alpha spacing
parameters.description: Bins in the radial height profile.

parameters.name: Minimum C-alphas per protomer
parameters.source_note: deposited entries often carry a short peptide that would otherwise be mistaken for a fourth subunit
parameters.description: Chain length below which a chain is not a protomer.

parameters.name: SASA probe radius
parameters.source_note: the standard water probe
parameters.description: Rolling-probe radius for solvent-accessible surface.

parameters.name: SASA sphere points
parameters.source_note: numerical quadrature density
parameters.description: Points per atom in the Shrake-Rupley quadrature.

parameters.name: Minimum sequence separation
parameters.source_note: excludes trivial i,i+1 backbone contacts
parameters.description: Residues closer than this in sequence are ignored.

parameters.name: Alpha-sphere minimum radius
parameters.source_note: fpocket's default
parameters.description: Smallest alpha sphere kept.

parameters.name: Alpha-sphere maximum radius
parameters.source_note: fpocket's default
parameters.description: Largest alpha sphere kept.

parameters.name: Burial neighbour count
parameters.source_note: without this filter the top pocket percolates over the whole surface at 408,000 A^3 across 601 residues
parameters.description: Protein atoms required near a sphere for it to count.

parameters.name: Burial neighbour radius
parameters.source_note: one shell beyond the largest alpha sphere, so burial is judged on contacting protein
parameters.description: Radius within which burial neighbours are counted.

parameters.name: Ligand contact cutoff
parameters.source_note: a heavy-atom contact distance; slightly beyond a hydrogen bond
parameters.description: Distance defining a residue-ligand contact.

parameters.name: Network contact cutoff
parameters.source_note: the standard C-alpha contact distance for residue networks; shorter than the ANM cutoff because a network edge is a contact, not a spring
parameters.description: C-alpha separation defining a network edge.

parameters.name: Minimum edge correlation
parameters.source_note: guards against log(0) in the edge weight
parameters.description: Correlation below which an edge is dropped.

parameters.name: Ortholog clade
parameters.source_note: 7742 = Vertebrata
parameters.description: Clade searched for orthologs.

parameters.name: Minimum ortholog coverage
parameters.source_note: below this a value measures the alignment rather than selection pressure on the residue
parameters.description: Fraction of orthologs that must align at a position.

parameters.name: Constrained-position threshold
parameters.source_note: a position must be this conserved to be called constrained when ranking candidates with no variant
parameters.description: Conservation above which a position counts as constrained.

parameters.name: SASA points, feature table
parameters.source_note: coarser quadrature for the 1279-residue feature table, where relative SASA is used as a rank rather than a value
parameters.description: Quadrature density when building the feature table.

parameters.name: Pore hydrophobicity contact radius
parameters.source_note: Kyte-Doolittle averaging radius for the legacy pore hydrophobicity profile; the CHAP path uses hydration.kernel_bandwidth instead
parameters.description: Radius within which lining residues are averaged.

parameters.name: Buriedness ray length
parameters.source_note: how far a cast ray looks for protein before calling that direction open
parameters.description: Ray length for buriedness.

parameters.name: Buriedness ray clearance
parameters.source_note: a ray passing within this of an atom centre counts as blocked; roughly a heavy-atom radius
parameters.description: Miss distance below which a ray is blocked.

parameters.name: Alpha-sphere cluster distance
parameters.source_note: single-linkage distance joining alpha spheres into one pocket
parameters.description: Clustering distance for pockets.

parameters.name: Pocket lining cutoff
parameters.source_note: distance from an alpha sphere within which a residue is called lining
parameters.description: Pocket lining distance.

parameters.name: Side-chain reach
parameters.source_note: a C-alpha network places contacts at C-alpha separation, but a side-chain change is felt by what the side chain touches; roughly an extended side-chain length
parameters.description: Distance over which a contact feels a side-chain change.

parameters.name: Packing weight
parameters.source_note: the original volume term, kept at unit weight so the new terms are additions rather than a reweighting
parameters.description: How strongly a volume change scales a contact.

parameters.name: Charge weight
parameters.source_note: an ENM spring is an effective stiffness standing in for packing, hydrogen bonds and ion pairs together; losing a salt bridge is a large fraction of a contact's stiffness
parameters.description: How strongly a charge change scales a contact to a charged partner.

parameters.name: Hydrogen-bond weight
parameters.source_note: weaker than the charge term because a hydrogen bond contributes less to an effective stiffness than an ion pair at the same separation
parameters.description: How strongly a change in donor/acceptor capacity scales a contact.

parameters.name: Proline backbone weight
parameters.source_note: proline restrains phi and removes a backbone donor, stiffening sequence-local contacts specifically
parameters.description: Stiffening applied to sequence-local contacts when proline is introduced.

parameters.name: Proline effect span
parameters.source_note: one turn of helix either side, the range over which a backbone restraint is felt
parameters.description: Sequence separation within which proline stiffens.

parameters.name: Glycine weight
parameters.source_note: negative: removing the side chain leaves nothing to mediate the contact, so it softens
parameters.description: Softening applied when glycine is introduced.

parameters.name: Minimum spring scale
parameters.source_note: a spring may weaken but never invert, or the quadratic form stops being an energy and the Hessian stops being positive semi-definite
parameters.description: Floor on the per-contact spring scale.

parameters.name: Minimum pair separation, distance-space overlap
parameters.source_note: pairs closer than this barely change length during the transition, so they add noise rather than signal to the distance-space correlation
parameters.description: Shortest C-alpha pair used in the superposition-free overlap.

parameters.name: Significance level
parameters.source_note: pre-registered for both variant tests
parameters.description: Type-I error rate.

parameters.name: Target power
parameters.source_note: the conventional 80%; both power statements in the project are quoted at it
parameters.description: Power at which the minimum detectable effect is quoted.

parameters.name: Permutation shuffles
parameters.source_note: p-values use the (r+1)/(n+1) convention, so they can never be exactly zero
parameters.description: Label shuffles.

parameters.name: Bootstrap resamples
parameters.source_note: 10k resamples give a percentile interval stable to about the third decimal
parameters.description: Resamples for the effect-size confidence interval.

parameters.name: HaloTag linker length
parameters.source_note: The construct this project is meant to describe does not state its linker, and neither does the halotag_binding_sim project it comes from. 10 residues is a mid-range flexible linker for a C-terminal fusion. It sets how far the tag can reach, so it is the single assumption the fusion geometry rests on and must be varied, not trusted.
parameters.description: Residues between PIEZO1's C-terminus and the HaloTag N-terminus.

parameters.name: Extension per linker residue
parameters.source_note: Ca-Ca rise of a fully extended polypeptide, the standard value. It is an upper bound: a real flexible linker is coiled and reaches less, so the envelope errs generous.
parameters.description: Maximum reach contributed by each linker residue.

parameters.name: Accessible-volume grid spacing
parameters.source_note: resolution of the envelope; finer costs cubically and does not change where the envelope sits
parameters.description: Grid step for sampling accessible tag positions.

parameters.name: Pore-mouth radius
parameters.source_note: how close to the conduction axis an atom must be to count as lining the cytosolic mouth rather than sitting on a blade. The CTD bundle is well inside it and the blades far outside, so the answer is flat in between; taking the lowest atom anywhere instead finds a blade tip and moves the pore exit by over 10 nm
parameters.description: Radius about the axis defining the cytosolic pore mouth.

parameters.name: Tag-channel clearance
parameters.source_note: added to the tag's own radius when rejecting positions, so contact rather than overlap is what is excluded
parameters.description: Extra clearance required between tag body and channel.

parameters.name: Tag-atom contact distance
parameters.source_note: twice Bondi's carbon van der Waals radius, so a pair at this separation is touching. It applies only to the drawn fold: it sets how many atoms are reported in contact with the channel and which of the undetermined spins is drawn, and changes no modelled position. The finding is insensitive to it — no spin is contact-free on 8YEZ, 7WLT or 11ZC anywhere from 2.0 to 4.0 A, except 7WLT below 3.4 A.
parameters.description: Separation below which a drawn tag atom counts as touching the channel.

parameters.name: HaloTag covalent on-rate
parameters.source_note: apparent second-order rate for the HaloTag-chloroalkane reaction, which is covalent and does not reverse
parameters.description: Second-order rate constant for ligand capture by one tag.

parameters.name: HaloTags per channel
parameters.source_note: PIEZO1 is a homotrimer, so a C-terminal fusion puts one tag on each protomer; this is the exponent in p^3
parameters.description: Independent labelling sites on one channel.

parameters.name: Ligand access rate, living cell
parameters.source_note: tau ~ 2 min for a cell-permeable JF dye to equilibrate across the plasma membrane. A model estimate in the source project too, not a measurement; it sets how much of the labelling lag is transport rather than chemistry.
parameters.description: Membrane permeation rate for the ligand in a live cell.

parameters.name: Ligand partition, living cell
parameters.source_note: JF dyes are cell-permeable, so intracellular concentration reaches the bath concentration at steady state
parameters.description: Steady-state intracellular / bath ligand concentration.

parameters.name: Reactive fraction of tags
parameters.source_note: assumed fully reactive in a living cell. It caps p, so the fully-labelled asymptote is active_fraction^3 and no incubation time can beat it; fixation is believed to lower it but this project has not measured that.
parameters.description: Fraction of tags chemically able to react.

parameters.name: Bath ligand concentration
parameters.source_note: 200 nM, the standard live-cell JF646 labelling condition
parameters.description: Applied ligand concentration in the bath.

parameters.name: Incubation time
parameters.source_note: 30 min, the standard live-cell labelling protocol
parameters.description: Ligand incubation time before wash.

parameters.name: Per-dye brightness CV
parameters.source_note: spread applied to each dye's contribution when turning integer dye counts into a predicted amplitude histogram; it decides whether the 1/2/3-dye levels stay resolvable
parameters.description: Coefficient of variation of one dye's brightness.

parameters.name: Temperature
parameters.source_note: 37 C, the condition PIEZO1 conductance is usually recorded at
parameters.description: Absolute temperature entering the thermal voltage.

parameters.name: Bath salt concentration
parameters.source_note: symmetric ~150 mM monovalent, the standard recording condition for the 25-30 pS figure
parameters.description: Symmetric bath concentration of the permeant salt.

parameters.name: Test voltage
parameters.source_note: 60 mV; small enough that the I-V is still linear, so the chord conductance equals the slope conductance
parameters.description: Voltage at which the conductance is evaluated.

parameters.name: Cation bulk diffusivity
parameters.source_note: K+ in water at 25 C; the standard tabulated value
parameters.description: Bulk diffusion coefficient of the permeant cation.

parameters.name: Anion bulk diffusivity
parameters.source_note: Cl- in water at 25 C; the standard tabulated value
parameters.description: Bulk diffusion coefficient of the counter-anion.

parameters.name: Calcium bulk diffusivity
parameters.source_note: Ca2+ in water at 25 C; slower than K+ because it is more strongly hydrated
parameters.description: Bulk diffusion coefficient of calcium.

parameters.name: Cation crystal radius
parameters.source_note: K+ Shannon radius. The crystal rather than hydrated radius, because an ion can shed water to cross a constriction - which is itself a modelling choice
parameters.description: Radius subtracted from the pore when computing access.

parameters.name: Anion crystal radius
parameters.source_note: Cl- Shannon radius
parameters.description: Anion crystal radius.

parameters.name: Calcium crystal radius
parameters.source_note: Ca2+ Shannon radius
parameters.description: Calcium crystal radius.

parameters.name: In-pore diffusivity scaling
parameters.source_note: Ions move more slowly in a pore than in bulk water, and by how much is not measured for PIEZO1. Together with the ion radius this is what the computed conductance is most sensitive to, so it must be swept, not trusted.
parameters.description: In-pore diffusivity as a fraction of the bulk value.

parameters.name: In-pore relative permittivity
parameters.source_note: water in a nanopore is less polarisable than in bulk (80); 40 is a common compromise. It only matters where there is fixed charge to screen.
parameters.description: Relative permittivity used in the Poisson equation.

parameters.name: Sodium bulk diffusivity
parameters.source_note: Na+ in water at 25 C; the standard tabulated value. Slower than K+ because it holds its hydration shell more tightly.
parameters.description: Bulk diffusion coefficient of sodium.

parameters.name: Sodium crystal radius
parameters.source_note: Na+ Shannon radius, six-coordinate
parameters.description: Sodium crystal radius.

parameters.name: Dilution potential, high side
parameters.source_note: 150 mM NaCl intracellular, the concentrated side of the protocol P_Cl/P_Na was measured with
parameters.description: Bath concentration on the concentrated side.

parameters.name: Dilution potential, dilute side
parameters.source_note: 30 mM NaCl extracellular (with sucrose for osmolarity), the dilute side of the same protocol
parameters.description: Bath concentration on the dilute side.

parameters.name: Published P_Cl/P_Na
parameters.source_note: mPiezo1 permeates chloride with P_Cl/P_Na = 0.14, from the dilution potential inverted through GHK. Below one, so the channel prefers cations — but far from zero, so it is a weakly selective cation channel and not an ion-exchange membrane.
parameters.description: Measured chloride-over-sodium permeability ratio.

parameters.name: Published unitary conductance
parameters.source_note: 25-30 pS for PIEZO1 with monovalent cations; the midpoint is the comparison target for the PNP model
parameters.description: Measured single-channel conductance.

parameters.name: Aspartate side-chain reach
parameters.source_note: Ca to carboxylate-carbon distance in an extended Asp, from standard side-chain geometry
parameters.description: How far Asp can put its charge from its own C-alpha.

parameters.name: Glutamate side-chain reach
parameters.source_note: one methylene longer than Asp
parameters.description: How far Glu can put its charge from its own C-alpha.

parameters.name: Lysine side-chain reach
parameters.source_note: Ca to NZ in an all-trans lysine
parameters.description: How far Lys can put its charge from its own C-alpha.

parameters.name: Arginine side-chain reach
parameters.source_note: Ca to the guanidinium centre in an extended arginine; the longest ionisable side chain there is
parameters.description: How far Arg can put its charge from its own C-alpha.

parameters.name: Axial charge smoothing
parameters.source_note: A charge's height along the axis is known to about a side-chain length, and on the open structure only from C-alpha. Placing it on a single slice would claim a precision the coordinates do not have and would make the density depend on the slice spacing. Total charge is conserved whatever this is set to.
parameters.description: Gaussian width each charge is spread over along the axis.

parameters.name: Counterion packing ceiling
parameters.source_note: Close-packed hydrated K+ at a 3.3 A radius is about 8 M, so 10 M is where a continuum treatment of point ions has certainly stopped describing a solution. It only ever flags a result — no calculation reads it as an input, and nothing is clipped to it.
parameters.description: In-pore concentration above which the model is flagged.

parameters.name: Gap anchor window
parameters.source_note: How many resolved residues either side of an unresolved stretch are used to place the prediction into it. Both flanks are required, so the fill is interpolated rather than cantilevered like the blade; the flank RMSD is reported so a bad fit is visible rather than absorbed.
parameters.description: Resolved residues each side of a gap used to anchor its fill.

parameters.name: Longest gap filled
parameters.source_note: A local fit at two flanks says nothing about what a very long insert does in between, and a 400-residue loop placed that way would look like structure. Gaps longer than this are left empty and counted, so the model reports what it did not fill.
parameters.description: Gaps longer than this are reported rather than filled.

parameters.name: Numbering identification floor
parameters.source_note: A deposited file's residue names must agree with the sequence its numbering belongs to at essentially every position. Measured across all 21 entries the winner scores 1.000 and the runner-up below 0.25, so anything under 0.9 means the file is not in the numbering it was matched to and the comparison must not proceed.
parameters.description: Identity below which a numbering identification is refused.

parameters.name: Numbering identification margin
parameters.source_note: A confident answer and a coin flip look identical once only the winner is reported. The measured margin is at least 0.75 on every entry, so half is a wide floor that would still catch a genuinely ambiguous file.
parameters.description: How far the best reference must beat the second.

parameters.name: Transmembrane boundary slack
parameters.source_note: How far outside a UniProt helix an aligned midpoint may land and still count as that helix. UniProt boundaries are predictions with a residue or two of play and the alignment adds its own. Measured: 37 of 38 helices agree, unchanged from 0 to 8 residues of slack; above that the count falls, and it falls because adjacent PIEZO2 helices sit as little as 2 residues apart, so wide windows overlap and the match stops being unique. That is a limit of the criterion, not a disagreement, and 5 sits in the middle of the flat range.
parameters.description: Tolerance when asking which helix an aligned residue is in.

parameters.name: Splice shift search range
parameters.source_note: How far a splice-isoform renumbering is searched for when the straight identification fails. The one case here is 6LQI at 24 residues; the range is wide because the search is only ever entered after a failure and a wrong answer is refused by requiring both halves to agree essentially perfectly.
parameters.description: Largest constant renumbering searched for after a splice site.

parameters.name: Mismatch block floor
parameters.source_note: How long a run of disagreeing residues must be before it is reported as a numbering fault rather than as real sequence difference. An engineered variant changes one residue and must not be flagged; the measured case is a block of 91 in four human entries, so ten is far from either.
parameters.description: Shortest run of disagreement reported as a block.

parameters.name: B-factor resolution floor
parameters.source_note: Below one distinct B-factor value per ten residues the column was refined in groups and cannot resolve per-residue mobility, so a correlation against it would measure the grouping rather than the network. Measured here: 3JAC and 6BPZ carry ~212 distinct values over ~2700 C-alphas and are the only entries this excludes.
parameters.description: Distinct B-factor values per residue below which an entry is refused rather than compared.

parameters.name: Cytosolic calcium diffusivity
parameters.source_note: 220 um^2/s in cytosol - roughly a third of the value in water, because cytosolic buffers and obstacles retard it
parameters.description: Effective diffusion coefficient of free Ca2+ in cytosol.

parameters.name: Buffer association rate
parameters.source_note: a fast mobile endogenous buffer; with the concentration below this sets the screening length
parameters.description: On-rate of the dominant cytosolic calcium buffer.

parameters.name: Free buffer concentration
parameters.source_note: ~100 uM free mobile buffer, a typical cytosolic value. Only the product k_on*[B] matters, through lambda.
parameters.description: Concentration of free calcium buffer in the cytosol.

parameters.name: Calcium sensor dissociation constant
parameters.source_note: ~0.2 uM for a BAPTA-based indicator; the threshold the nanodomain is compared against
parameters.description: Kd of the BAPTA-based calcium sensor on the tag.

parameters.name: Calcium share of the unitary current
parameters.source_note: PIEZO1 is weakly cation-selective; the PNP model gives under 5% at 2 mM Ca2+. Not measured for this channel, and it scales the nanodomain linearly, so it is swept.
parameters.description: Fraction of the single-channel current carried by Ca2+.

parameters.name: Resting cytosolic calcium
parameters.source_note: ~100 nM, the standard resting cytosolic level; the baseline the nanodomain sits on top of
parameters.description: Bulk resting free calcium concentration.

parameters.name: Bilayer thickness
parameters.source_note: Figure 7a: 'a semi-sphere-shaped membrane 3.6 nm thick', idealised from the curved micelle density. Sets only where the two leaflet surfaces are drawn relative to the mid-plane; no area or energy in the dome model depends on it, because Helfrich theory works on the mid-plane.
parameters.description: Thickness of the bilayer the dome carries.

parameters.name: Idealised dome centre height
parameters.source_note: Figure 7a: the mid-plane semi-sphere 'is centered 4.0 nm above the projection plane'. With the 10.2 nm radius it fixes every other number in Figure 7-figure supplement 1 — an 18.8 nm opening, a 6.2 nm depth, 397 nm^2 of surface and 277 nm^2 projected. Raising it flattens the cap and shrinks the released area towards zero.
parameters.description: Height of the idealised sphere's centre above the plane.

parameters.name: Bilayer lytic tension
parameters.source_note: The scale Guo & MacKinnon quote their 42 k_BT stabilisation against: one tenth of lytic tension acting through 120 nm^2. Rawicz et al. 2000 measure rupture tensions of 5-10 mN/m across chain lengths; 3.5 k_BT/nm^2 is 14.4 mN/m, at the top of that range, so the 42 k_BT is an optimistic figure and is reported as one.
parameters.description: Tension at which a bilayer ruptures.

parameters.name: Hydropathy window
parameters.source_note: Kyte & Doolittle recommend 19-21 for identifying membrane-spanning segments and 7-11 for surface exposure. 19 is the shorter of the two membrane values, so it resolves the 4-TM repeat rather than smoothing it into one broad hydrophobic block.
parameters.description: Sliding-window width for the hydropathy average.

parameters.name: Transmembrane call threshold
parameters.source_note: Kyte & Doolittle's own figures place the membrane-spanning cut at a window average near +1.6 on the same scale. It is a threshold on a smoothed curve, not a prediction method: raising it loses genuine TM segments before it removes false ones, which is measured against UniProt's 38 rather than asserted.
parameters.description: Window hydropathy above which a segment is called TM.

parameters.name: Shortest TM call
parameters.source_note: a run shorter than this cannot cross a 3.6 nm bilayer as an alpha helix (1.5 A rise per residue gives 22.5 A at 15 residues, against a 36 A bilayer, so this is already generous and admits tilted and interfacial helices)
parameters.description: Minimum run length above threshold to call a segment.

parameters.name: Ionic strength
parameters.source_note: Figure 4c states 'aqueous solution containing 150 mM NaCl'. It enters only through the Debye length (7.86 A at this value), so it sets how quickly the surface potential decays, not its sign anywhere.
parameters.description: Bulk 1:1 salt concentration screening the surface.

parameters.name: Solvent permittivity
parameters.source_note: water at 298 K, the value APBS uses by default and the one Figure 4c will have been computed with
parameters.description: Relative permittivity of the aqueous phase.

parameters.name: Electrostatics temperature
parameters.source_note: 25 C, the default APBS calculations are reported at. The paper does not state a temperature; the Debye length moves by 2% between 25 and 37 C, which is invisible on a coloured surface.
parameters.description: Temperature entering the Debye length and the k_BT unit.

parameters.name: Surface potential scale
parameters.source_note: Figure 4c's colour bar runs -5 to +5 k_BT/e. Reproducing the panel means reproducing its saturation points too: a wider scale makes any surface look neutral and a narrower one makes any surface look charged.
parameters.description: Potential at which the red/blue surface colouring saturates.

parameters.name: Charge interaction cutoff
parameters.source_note: screened Coulomb falls as exp(-r/lambda_D)/r, so a cutoff is what makes the sum over 6B3R's 804 formal charges and 135k surface points tractable. The truncation error is measured rather than argued: against the exact all-pairs sum on 6B3R's own surface, 30 A costs at most 0.089 k_BT/e (2.2% of the peak) and no point moves by more than 0.1, while 20 A costs 0.30 (7.5%) and moves 19% of points that far. A first draft of this note claimed 'under 0.2%' from the analytic falloff alone and was an order of magnitude out, because the falloff bounds one charge and not 804.
parameters.description: Range beyond which a point charge is ignored.

parameters.name: Projection pixel size
parameters.source_note: the calibrated physical pixel size of the K2 data in the Methods, so a simulated projection is sampled the way the real 2D class averages were
parameters.description: Sampling of the simulated projection image.

parameters.name: Projection resolution
parameters.source_note: a 2D class average is not at the map's global resolution; 8 A reproduces the blurred, secondary-structure-free appearance of Figure 2a,b. It is a display choice and the panel is labelled a simulation rather than a class average because of it.
parameters.description: Gaussian blur applied to the simulated projection.

parameters.name: Cross-helix minimum tilt
parameters.source_note: Guo & MacKinnon describe the cross-helices as running 'perpendicular to the TM helices' but give no residue ranges anywhere in the paper, so this reproduces their yellow helices by the property they are named for. 55 degrees from the local membrane normal separates them from transmembrane helices, which in this structure tilt up to about 40; the count is reported against the threshold so a reader can see how sharp the separation is rather than trusting the cut.
parameters.description: Tilt from the membrane normal above which a linker helix is called a cross-helix.

parameters.name: Micelle shell thickness
parameters.source_note: How far outside the hydrophobic belt the modelled detergent envelope is drawn. Chosen so the envelope's overall width matches the micelle in Figure 4b rather than derived from digitonin's dimensions, which the paper does not give — so it sets the *thickness* of the drawn shell and nothing else. The curvature reported with it is fitted to the belt atoms themselves and does not depend on this value at all, which is the point: an offset surface has the same centre and a radius larger by exactly the offset.
parameters.description: Offset of the modelled micelle surface from the belt.

parameters.name: Micelle grid spacing
parameters.source_note: marching-cubes resolution. Costs cubically and changes how faceted the surface looks, not where it is; the enclosed volume is stable to under a percent between 1.2 and 2.4 A, which is measured rather than assumed.
parameters.description: Grid step for contouring the micelle envelope.

parameters.name: Alpha-helix rise per residue
parameters.source_note: C-alpha advance along the helix axis per residue. With the 100-degree turn this gives 3.6 residues and 5.4 A per turn, the standard alpha helix. The detector is calibrated against an analytically generated helix at exactly these values before it is used on coordinates.
parameters.description: Axial rise per residue of an alpha helix.

parameters.name: Alpha-helix C-alpha radius
parameters.source_note: distance of a C-alpha from the helix axis; with the rise it separates an alpha helix from a 3-10 (1.9 A) and a pi helix (2.8 A)
parameters.description: Radial offset of C-alpha from the alpha-helix axis.

parameters.name: Alpha-helix turn per residue
parameters.source_note: rotation about the axis between consecutive residues, right-handed. This is the criterion that excludes a random coil: rise and radius alone passed 41% of the windows of a synthetic random walk, because a walk with a fixed step length looks locally like a helix on both.
parameters.description: Rotation per residue about the alpha-helix axis.

parameters.name: Helix rise tolerance
parameters.source_note: wide enough for a real, bent, 3.7-A-resolution helix and narrow enough that a 3-10 helix (2.0 A rise) falls outside it; the measured margin on 3-10 is 0.05 A, so this is the tightest of the three criteria
parameters.description: Permitted departure from the ideal helix rise.

parameters.name: Helix radius tolerance
parameters.source_note: deliberately loose: at 3.7 A resolution a C-alpha position carries most of an Angstrom of uncertainty, and the turn criterion is what does the discriminating
parameters.description: Permitted departure from the ideal C-alpha radius.

parameters.name: Helix turn tolerance
parameters.source_note: applied to the *worst* step in a window rather than the mean, so one reversal cannot hide inside an average. At 25 degrees a 3-10 helix (120) and a pi helix (87) are both excluded and every window of an ideal alpha helix is admitted.
parameters.description: Permitted departure from the ideal turn, worst step.

parameters.name: Helix detection window
parameters.source_note: just under two turns, the shortest window in which the turn criterion has enough steps to mean anything. It slides one residue at a time, so a bent helix is still recognised along its length rather than failing as a whole.
parameters.description: Sliding-window width for the helix criteria.

parameters.name: Histidine formal charge
parameters.source_note: At pH 7.4 a typical histidine (pKa ~6.0) is about 10% protonated. Zero is used rather than 0.1 because a fractional formal charge is not a state any single residue is in, and assigning a full +1 would put three spurious positive charges per protomer on the surface Figure 4c is read from. `compare_conventions` reports the effect of both alternatives rather than hiding the choice.
parameters.description: Charge placed on histidine when building formal charges.

parameters.name: First pore-proximal helix
parameters.source_note: TM25 opens THU7, the most distal 4-TM unit every deposited PIEZO1 entry in this project's catalogue resolves in all three protomers. Measured from the downloaded entries rather than chosen: it is the split that makes two entries comparable, and 6B3R resolves TM13-38 where 6BPZ resolves only TM25-38.
parameters.description: Helix index dividing the distal blade from the pore module for coverage-matched comparisons.

parameters.name: Cross-helix minimum length
parameters.source_note: two turns of alpha helix; shorter runs are single turns and loop fragments whose axis direction is not meaningful, and admitting them adds orientation noise rather than helices
parameters.description: Shortest helical run admitted as a cross-helix.
